question: Can you upgrade a wastewater plant's switchgear?
html:
Wastewater plant switchgear upgrades

Yes. Electrical work at wastewater plants is a core focus for us, led by our Connecticut team at Horton Electrical Services. The data below shows where we work. It does not list past switchgear jobs, so ask us for specific project references.

Who does the work

  • Horton Electrical Services (Canton and Collinsville, CT) joined CET on Sep 15, 2026. It brought Connecticut wastewater relationships and more than 100 field staff plus 20 managers (CET public filings).
  • NuWave Energy Solutions (Norwell, MA) adds energy-efficiency work. Aeration is often a plant's largest energy load (CET wastewater-plant targets).
  • CET holds electrical licensing in six states (CET growth plan).

Where we are focused

We track 183 plants across CT, MA and RI. We are pursuing 62 funded or requested plant and pump-station projects (CET wastewater-plant targets; CET growth plan).

PlantFlowFunded or listed project
New Haven East Shore, CT40 MGD$82M wet-weather and odor-control upgrade, plus a $19.2M process-air-compressor request
Hartford WPCF, CT60 MGD$24.3M sludge screening and equalization, plus $31.6M in pump-station requests
Norwalk WPCF, CT18 MGD$26M final settling tanks, plus a $48M aeration request
MWRA Deer Island, MAnot listed$289M Clarifier #2 in the 2026 funding plan

Source: CET wastewater-plant targets, generated Sep 24, 2026. Connecticut Table 3 items are requests, not funded projects. Rhode Island figures come from a June 2026 draft list.

How a project usually fits

  • Most plant upgrades include electrical scope. Our data does not break out the switchgear share of any project. Bid documents or engineer's estimates would show it.
  • At Deer Island, the plant already generates 26% of its own electricity. Our role there is electrical subcontracting plus storage and efficiency (CET wastewater-plant targets).
  • We also plan to offer SCADA and pump-station monitoring as ongoing service (CET growth plan).

For a specific plant, share the single-line diagram, equipment age and the project timeline. We can then scope the work. We do not give regulatory or permit advice.

Switchgear work gets us inside the plant's electrical room, which is the natural lead-in to the monitoring and efficiency contracts that turn one-off bids into recurring revenue, the service mix PKF and Capstone value at 3 or more turns above project-heavy contractors (CET growth plan).

Next actions

  1. Compile Horton's past switchgear and motor-control project references for New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk outreach.
  2. Pull bid documents for the 62 tracked projects and tag those with electrical distribution scope. This replaces guesswork on switchgear value.
  3. Pair each switchgear pitch with a NuWave aeration-efficiency offer at Norwalk and East Shore.
  4. Cross-check the target list against the EPA wastewater-plant compliance snapshot (Nov 9, 2026) to see which plants have expired or administratively continued permits. Use this only as timing context.
